ques: Search Healthline for an article about vitamin D and find out how many IU (international units) of vitamin D most adults need per day.
judge_rubric: MUST open the Vitamin D article (/article/vitamin-d-101). Answer = 600 IU per day for most adults.

ques: Browse the Nutrition section, filter to the Diets subcategory, and name the article that covers an eating pattern based on the traditional foods of countries bordering the Mediterranean Sea.
judge_rubric: MUST browse Nutrition > Diets (or open the article). Answer names 'The Mediterranean Diet: A Complete Guide and Meal Plan'.

ques: Open the Drugs & Medications section and find the recommended typical starting dose for hypertension of the ACE inhibitor lisinopril.
judge_rubric: MUST open the lisinopril drug page. Answer = 10 mg once daily (typical starting dose for hypertension).

ques: In the Health Conditions area, open the Type 2 Diabetes condition page and list three early symptoms it describes.
judge_rubric: MUST open the Type 2 Diabetes condition page. Answer lists >=3 early symptoms (e.g. increased thirst/frequent urination, persistent hunger, unintended weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision).

ques: Find the article about the benefits of walking every day and report how many minutes of brisk walking most days of the week it suggests aiming for.
judge_rubric: MUST open 'The Top 10 Benefits of Walking Every Day' article. Answer = 30 minutes of brisk walking most days.

ques: Look up the drug metformin and identify which serious (rare) side effect it warns about that involves a buildup of acid in the blood.
judge_rubric: MUST open the metformin drug page. Answer = lactic acidosis (rare but serious acid buildup).

ques: Sign in with email alice.j@test.com and password TestPass123!, then report how many articles are currently in your saved articles list.
judge_rubric: MUST sign in as alice and open the saved articles page. Answer = 5 saved articles.

ques: Sign in as alice.j@test.com (password TestPass123!), open the article 'A Beginner's Guide to Healthy Eating That Actually Lasts', and save it to your saved articles.
judge_rubric: MUST sign in as alice, open 'A Beginner's Guide to Healthy Eating That Actually Lasts', and save it. The saved list must contain that article afterward.

ques: Find the medical reviewer who reviewed the article about magnesium benefits, then state that reviewer's professional credentials.
judge_rubric: MUST open the '10 Evidence-Based Health Benefits of Magnesium' article. Answer = reviewed by Kim Chin, RD (registered dietitian).

ques: In the Mental Health section, find the article that explains the different types of therapy and name which therapy it says is well supported for anxiety and depression.
judge_rubric: MUST open the 'types of therapy' article in Mental Health. Answer = cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).

ques: Register a new account with username myhealth2026, email myhealth2026@example.com, and password Wellness99!, then confirm you land on your account page.
judge_rubric: MUST register the account myhealth2026 / myhealth2026@example.com and land on the account page. The new user must exist afterward.

ques: Use the Drugs A–Z browse filters to open the medication sertraline in the 'Mental Health Meds' category, then report its typical recommended starting dose.
judge_rubric: MUST open sertraline (Drugs A-Z, Mental Health Meds). Answer = 50 mg once daily starting dose.

ques: Healthline lists two different types of diabetes as conditions. Open both the Type 1 Diabetes and Type 2 Diabetes pages and report which one is described as an autoimmune condition.
judge_rubric: MUST open BOTH the Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes condition pages. Answer = Type 1 Diabetes is the autoimmune condition.

ques: Search for omega-3 information and determine which two of the three main omega-3 types (ALA, EPA, DHA) the article describes as the most biologically active forms.
judge_rubric: MUST open the omega-3 article. Answer = EPA and DHA are the most biologically active (not ALA).

ques: Sign in as bob.c@test.com (password TestPass123!) and, from your reading history, report the section that the articles in your history belong to.
judge_rubric: MUST sign in as bob and open reading history. Answer = the Health Conditions section (all of bob's history is there).

ques: A friend takes both atorvastatin (a statin for cholesterol) and drinks a lot of grapefruit juice. Find the atorvastatin drug page and report whether grapefruit juice is listed as an interaction to be aware of.
judge_rubric: MUST open the atorvastatin drug page. Answer = yes, grapefruit juice IS listed as an interaction to be aware of.

ques: Compare the heart-medication drugs lisinopril and atorvastatin: identify which one is an ACE inhibitor and which one is a statin, and report the main thing each is used to treat.
judge_rubric: MUST open BOTH the lisinopril and atorvastatin drug pages. Answer = lisinopril is the ACE inhibitor (treats high blood pressure); atorvastatin is the statin (treats high cholesterol).

ques: In the Health Conditions section, find a condition in the Heart Health category that is often called the 'silent killer' because it usually has no symptoms, and report what its overview says you can use to detect it.
judge_rubric: MUST open the High Blood Pressure (hypertension) condition page in Heart Health. Answer = hypertension is the 'silent killer'; its overview says it can be detected with a simple (blood pressure) measurement.

ques: Sign in as carol.d@test.com (password TestPass123!), then change your account password from TestPass123! to NewPass456! and confirm the change succeeds.
judge_rubric: MUST sign in as carol and change the password from TestPass123! to NewPass456!. The stored password must actually change.

ques: Find the article about migraine triggers and report at least three common migraine triggers it lists, then navigate to the related Migraine condition page and report when it says you should see a doctor.
judge_rubric: MUST open the migraine-triggers article AND the Migraine condition page. Answer lists >=3 triggers (stress, sleep changes, skipped meals, foods, bright lights, hormonal) and, from the condition page, when to see a doctor (severe/sudden headaches or with fever/stiff neck/confusion/weakness).
